title: Visualizing and manipulating the production and accumulation of hyaluronan for functional assessment in chicken embryos
protocol: Weigh 200 mg of resin beads into a 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Wash the beads three times with 1 mL of 1× PBS.
Centrifuge the beads at 5,000 G for 1 minute after each wash to remove PBS.
Wash the beads three times in DMSO for 1 minute each.
Incubate the beads in a 40 mM solution of MU-Xyl (in DMSO) for 12 hours at 4°C with gentle rotation.
Add 2.5 μL of drawing ink to 100 μL of the soaked bead mix.
Incubate the mixture for another 2 hours at 25°C.
Bring the eggs out of the incubator one at a time.
Place the eggs on an egg tray.
Remove the cellophane tape window with scissors to access the embryo.
Add 5–10 drops of 1× PBS with 1× Penicillin-Streptomycin (PBS/PS).
Remove the vitelline membrane from the top of the embryo (HH14-16) using a 21G needle.
Make a clean incision along the somatic mesoderm using Dumont #5 forceps.
Gently pipette 10 μL of bead mix onto the embryo near the site of the incision with access to the coelomic cavity.
Insert beads one at a time into the cavity using Dumont #5 forceps.
Add a few drops of PBS/PS on top of the embryo to ensure that the beads are lodged correctly.
Seal the egg with cellophane tape and return it to the incubator until the desired stage.
Cut around the extra-embryonic vasculature to free the embryo.
Collect the embryo into a petri dish with ice-cold 1× PBS using the perforated spoon.
Remove any remaining extraembryonic membranes and yolk from the embryo using forceps and spring scissors.
Transfer the embryo into ice-cold 2% paraformaldehyde in 1× PBS to fix for 12 hours at 4°C.
Wash the embryos three times with 1× PBS for 5 minutes each while agitating on a nutator.
Screen the embryos under a dissection microscope for gross morphological anomalies and exclude anomalous embryos from further analysis.
Microinject DNA of interest into the coelomic cavity of a chicken embryo.
Position positive and negative electrodes around the injected area for electroporation.
Electroporate the right (or left) splanchnic mesoderm to target the DM precursor.
Bring the eggs out of the incubator onto an egg tray one at a time.
Remove the cellophane tape window with scissors to access the embryo.
Add 5–10 drops of 1× PBS with 1× Penicillin-Streptomycin (PBS/PS).
Remove the vitelline membrane from the top the embryo using a 21G needle.
Inject 0.1 μL–0.2 μL of the plasmid or morpholino electroporation mix into the coelomic cavity, on the left or the right side of the embryo.
Introduce the electroporation mix into the left coelomic cavity to induce gene expression in the left side of the DM.
Position the negative electrode directly above the injected coelomic cavity and the positive electrode under the non-injected coelomic cavity.
Deliver 3 square pulses (50 mV, 10 ms) using the square wave electroporator.
Seal the egg window with cellophane tape.
Return the egg for incubation until the desired stage.
Induce HA-modifying enzyme expression under TRE promoter with doxycycline.
Electroporate the embryonic splanchnic mesoderm at HH15 stage with constructs targeting HA-modifying enzymes.
Induce expression of HA-modifying enzymes by adding doxycycline at HH20 stage after DM formation.
Monitor H2B-RFP expression to confirm electroporation in the right DM.
Observe GFP expression upon doxycycline induction at HH20, indicating activation of bidirectional tetracycline-responsive promoter.
Assess loss of HA accumulation within the left DM when Hyal2 is expressed under the construct by HH21.
Electroporate plasmid constructs as specified.
Mix plasmids with a concentration ratio of 2:1:2 to ensure a total DNA concentration not exceeding 2.0 μg/μL.
Add 500 μL of doxycycline solution (0.1 μg/μL) in drops on top of the embryo for inducing expression under the TRE-promoter.
Collect embryos as described in Part I, steps 3a–d.
Sort collected embryos accordingly.
Fix sorted embryos for further analysis.
Carefully examine embryos for gross morphological anomalies after electroporation.
Discard embryos with developmental defects in non-targeted areas.
Dissect out limb buds from both sides of the embryo carefully.
Examine the posterior body wall for expression of the electroporated fluorescence reporter.
Dissect out gut dorsal mesentery from both sides of the embryo.
Exclude embryos without proper targeting of the DM or tissue of interest.
Compare targeted embryos to similarly targeted negative controls.
Optimize tissue-specific staging for dynamic morphogenetic processes affected by targeting.
Use 3 pulses of 50 mV and 10 ms for electroporation in the embryonic DM/splanchnic mesoderm.
Consider embryos with >70% GFP+ tissue area for analysis.
Store PFA fixed embryos in 1×PBS for up to one week.
Store cryo-embedded embryos at −80°C for up to one year.
Reconstitute HABP by adding 100 μL of double-distilled water to 50 mg of HABP.
Vortex the vial and incubate at 20°C–25°C for 20 min.
Vortex again after incubation.
Make aliquots of 10 μL each from the reconstituted solution.
Store the aliquots at -80°C for up to a year.
Rehydrate cryosections of OCT-embedded tissues in 1×PBS with 2 washes of 5 min each.
Wash slides in 1×PBST (1×PBS with 0.03% Tween 20).
Place slides in a humidified slide chamber and cover tissue sections with HABP blocking solution.
Incubate slides at 20°C–25°C for 45 min.
Decant blocking solution onto a paper towel.
Add 200μL of HABP solution (1:40 diluted in blocking solution) to cover the slide.
Wash slides 3 times in 1× PBST for 5 min each.
Add Streptavidin-Alexa Fluor conjugate secondary antibody and DAPI solutions onto the slides.
Incubate slides at 20°C–25°C in the dark for 45 min.
Wash slides 3 times in 1× PBST and once with autoclaved double-distilled or reverse-osmosis water for 5 min each.
Mount the sections on slides with a coverslip using ProLong Gold Antifade mounting medium.
Store the slides at 4°C after the mounting medium has dried for 24 hours in the dark.
Image the slides within a week of preparation.
Embed paraformaldehyde-fixed tissue in paraffin.
Obtain 6–10 μm thick sections from the embedded tissue.
Dry the sections for 12–16 hours at 37°C.
Bake the slides for 20 minutes at 60°C followed by a 10-minute cooldown.
Wash the slides twice with 100% Xylene for 10 minutes each.
Wash the slides sequentially in ethanol gradients (100%, 75%, 50%, and 25%) for 10 minutes each.
Wash the slides twice with water.
Transfer slides into diluted Antigen retrieval solution (1 mL of antigen unmasking solution, citrate-based in 100 mL of water).
Microwave the container to boiling point.
Allow the slide jar to cool down at 4°C for 20 minutes before proceeding.
Follow the protocol from Part III, step 8b after cooling.
Reconstitute hyaluronidase to a concentration of 0.2 Units/μL in 100 mM Sodium acetate buffer (pH6.0).
Incubate the reconstituted hyaluronidase at 20°C–25°C for 20 min.
Aliquot the reconstituted hyaluronidase and store at −80°C.
Rehydrate slides with PBS between Part III, steps 8b and 8c.
Treat slides with 100 mM Sodium acetate buffer (pH6.0) for 15 min at 37°C.
Dab the slides on a paper towel to remove the buffer.
Apply the reconstituted hyaluronidase solution (0.2 Units/μL) to cover the tissue sections.
Incubate the tissue sections with the hyaluronidase solution for 2 h at 60°C.
Wash the tissue sections with 1×PBS after incubation.
Replace HABP with water during the primary HABP incubation (Part III, step 8d) to serve as a negative control.
Use Bouin’s fixative for preserving the architecture of tissue expansion induced by hyaluronan.
Handle picric acid with care and caution due to its potential explosiveness.
Transfer Bouin’s fixative from the storage container into a glass vial, working inside a fume hood.
Collect embryos into the Bouin’s fixative and allow them to shake on a nutator for 2 h at 20°C–25°C.
Remove Bouin’s fixative carefully and wash the embryos three times for 10 min each with 70% ethanol while shaking on a nutator.
Discard yellow-colored ethanol according to institutional safety guidelines.
Continue washing the embryos, replacing the 70% ethanol hourly until clear.
Transfer into 100% ethanol for complete dehydration.
